candidateAudit.text: 🎶 Grätzel Jazz – Interkultureller Jazzdialog in Neubau Ein musikalisches Fest der Vielfalt und Nachbarschaft im 7*Stern Wohnzimmer! Erlebt einen Konzertabend, der musikalische Grenzen auflöst und das Grätzel zusammenbringt! Im ersten Teil des Abends entführt euch das herausragende Trio rund um Urs Hager, Kristian Lind und Esad Halilovic in eine Welt, in der moderner Jazz, traditionelles Liedgut und orientalische Rhythmen zu einem einzigartigen Klang verschmelzen. Feinfühlig begleitet wird das Set von Alena Baich, die mit Rezitationen und Moderation inhaltliche Brücken schlägt. Nach einer kurzen Pause heißt es dann: Bühne frei für das Grätzel! Im zweiten Teil des Abends öffnet sich das Konzert für eine nachbarschaftliche Jam-Session. Unter dem Motto „Sing deinen Lieblingssong / Bring dein Instrument“ laden wir Musiker:innen, Anrainer:innen und das Publikum ein, gemeinsam mit dem Trio den musikalischen Raum zu gestalten. Egal ob Profi, Hobby-Musiker:in oder begeisterte:r Zuhörer:in – feiert mit uns die lebendige Kultur in Neubau! 📅 Samstag, 21. November 2026 🕗 20:00 Uhr (Einlass 19:30) 📍 Café 7*Stern Wohnzimmer, Siebensterngasse 31, 1070 Wien 🎟️ Pay as you wish (freie Spende) #graetzeljazz #neubau #wien jazz jamsession interkulturell cafe7stern livemusik

candidateAudit.text: … ✨ Gestern Abend haben wir die Ausstellung TEMPORÄR. STRUKTUREN DER NOTWENDIGKEIT feierlich eröffnet – und gemeinsam mit euch den Auftakt gefeiert! Die Ausstellung widmet sich den oft übersehenen temporären Strukturen unserer Städte: von Baugerüsten und Schutzkonstruktionen bis hin zu provisorischen Infrastrukturen, die unseren Alltag am Laufen halten. Sie zeigt, welches Potenzial in diesen pragmatischen, flexiblen und oft überraschenden Lösungen steckt. Ein herzliches Dankeschön an alle, die dabei waren und diesen Abend mit uns so besonders gemacht haben! ❤️ 📸 Pics: esel.at, Hannah Mayr ********* ✨ Last night, we celebrated the opening of TEMPORÄR. STRUKTUREN DER NOTWENDIGKEIT! The exhibition explores the temporary structures that shape our cities and everyday lives – from scaffolding and protective structures to provisional infrastructures and the potential they hold. A big thank you to everyone who joined us and made the evening so special! ❤️

candidateAudit.title: Auf der Suche nach einer Frühstücksidee, die Groß und Klein schmeckt? ☺️ Diese Pancakes mit Zimt und Birne sind einfach gemacht und perfekt für einen gemütlichen Frühstücksmorgen m
candidateAudit.text: Auf der Suche nach einer Frühstücksidee, die Groß und Klein schmeckt? ☺️ Diese Pancakes mit Zimt und Birne sind einfach gemacht und perfekt für einen gemütlichen Frühstücksmorgen mit der ganzen Familie. 🍐🥞 Im Teig und zum Ausbacken verwenden wir unser mild-fruchtiges natives Bio-Olivenöl extra „Der Familienheld“ – getoppt werden die Pancakes mit warmen Birnen und Walnüssen. Natürlich könnt ihr eure Lieblingstoppings wählen✨ 🍐Du brauchst: (2 Portionen) 250 g Dinkelmehl 1 TL Backpulver 1 TL Zimt 1 Prise Salz 2 Bio-Eier aus Freilandhaltung 180 ml Mandeldrink 2 EL MANI Bläuel „Der Familienheld“ natives Olivenöl extra + etwas mehr zum Braten 1 kleine Birne, gerieben 1 TL Ahornsirup Topping: 2 Birnen gewürfelt/ in Spalten 1 EL MANI Bläuel „Der Familienheld“ natives Olivenöl extra 1 TL Zimt etwas Vanille (optional) Walnüsse Ahornsirup 👩🏼‍🍳So geht‘s: Trockene Zutaten mischen. Eier, Milch, Vanille und Öl verrühren und kurz unterheben. Geriebene birne dazugeben. Den Teig ca. 10 Minuten ruhen lassen. Bei Bedarf etwas Wasser hinzufügen – der Teig sollte dickflüssig sein. Birnen in Spalten oder würfelig schneiden und mit Olivenöl, Vanille und Zimt kurz anbraten. Bei Bedarf etwas Wasser hinzufügen. Pancakes bei mittlerer Hitze in etwas Olivenöl goldbraun ausbacken. Pancakes mit warmem Birnen-Topping, Walnüssen und Ahornsirup servieren. #pancakes #familienrezepte #manibläuel #dinkelpancakes kochenmitolivenöl

candidateAudit.text: ROOTS MUSIC FROM Southern Africa 14TH EDITION JAZZMED wurde 2006 von Thomas Pfleger gemeinsam mit Stefan Pelzl und Robert Schönherr gegründet. Die Eigenkompositionen orientieren sich musikalisch an R&B, Pop,Latin Jazz und souligen Stilelementen und klingen gleichermaßen melodisch wie groovig. Gemeinsam mit ihren Special Guests des Abends -Stefanie Pitsch, und Vusa Mkhaya lädt JAZZMED zu einem festlichen Abend voller musikalische Vielfalt und Emotion. Das Publikum erwartet eine stimmungsvolle Mischung aus Jazz, R’n’B, Latin, Pop und Funk – feinfühlig, groovend un voller Lebensfreude. Besetzung: Thomas Pfleger: guitar, Stefan Pelzl: alto saxophone, flute, Wolfgang Schuller: bass, Robert Schönherr: piano, Werner Mras: drums Special Guests: Stefanie Pitsch: vocals, Vusa Mkhaya: vocals Blessings Nqo Nkomo & Rhythms Afro Band Blessings „Nqo“ Nkomo is a Zimbabwean musician, composer, and vocalist known for his work in world music and traditional African genres. Based in Vienna, Austria, he has built an international career both as a solo artist and as a member of several prominent musical groups. Musical Groups Insingizi: Nqo is a founding member of this award-winning a cappella trio, which specializes in the traditional „Imbube“ style of Southern Africa. MoZuluArt: A collaborative project that fuses traditional Zulu music with classical compositions, particularly those of Mozart. The group was founded by Nqo alongside Vusa Mkhaya Ndlovu, Ramadu, and Roland Guggenbichler. Musical Fusion: His work blends traditional a cappella with gospel and world music. candidateAudit.title: JULIJAN ERIC & MIDNIGHT LIGHTNIN‘ (Channeling the Spirit of Hendrix from Europe) Midnight Lightnin‘ ist die Band, in der Jimi spielen würde, wenn er noch da wäre. In dieser Band ko
candidateAudit.text: JULIJAN ERIC & MIDNIGHT LIGHTNIN‘ (Channeling the Spirit of Hendrix from Europe) Midnight Lightnin‘ ist die Band, in der Jimi spielen würde, wenn er noch da wäre. In dieser Band kommt sein freier Geist voll zur Geltung. Wie du dir denken kannst, ist der Gitarrist Julijan der Hauptprotagonist. Manchmal kann jemand so ein reiches Erbe ganz locker tragen. Er spielt seine Soli nicht wie dogmatische Texte, sondern redet während der Jams mit seiner Gitarre, so wie Jimi es gemacht hat. Es muss nicht alles perfekt sein, das war es in den 60ern auch nicht. Wichtig war der Ausdruck, und Julijan geht sanft mit seiner Gitarre um, selbst wenn er sie mit den Zähnen spielt. Ein zusätzlicher Bonus ist, dass er tatsächlich den Verstärker spielt, der von einem Hendrix-Verstärkertechniker aus den USA gebaut wurde. Jimi hatte Mitch, Buddy, Billy und Noel und all die anderen coolen Leute von damals. Julijan hat Zlatko, Miha und andere coole Leute von heute. „Sie sind es, die Midnight Lightnin‘ möglich machen, sie sind Teil der Magie“, sagt Julijan Eric. Und sie kommen alle aus einem kleinen Land namens Slowenien. „Manchmal ist es schwer zu glauben, dass es in einem Land mit nur zwei Millionen Einwohnern jemanden gibt, der allein durch sein Erscheinen auf der Bühne das Gefühl vermittelt, dass wir gleich einen von Jimi’s Songs spielen werden. Und ich spreche natürlich von Julijan“, erklärt Zlatko Djogic, der Schlagzeuger. You can listen to the greatest hits and at the same time every concert is unique Zlatko Djogic – Schlagzeug, Miha Ribaric- Bass und Julijan Eric – Gitarre und Gesang

candidateAudit.text: ♏️ Pflanzen des Skorpions – für Tiefe, Wandlung & innere Kraft Der Skorpion geht dorthin, wo andere lieber an der Oberfläche bleiben. Er steht für Transformation, Intuition, Sexualität, Regeneration, Macht und Loslassen – und genau diese Themen spiegeln sich auch in seiner Pflanzenwelt wider. Zu den besonders passenden Pflanzen gehören: Blauer Lotus – für Intuition und innere Tiefe Reishi – für Ruhe, Regeneration und seelische Tiefe Brennnessel – für klare Grenzen und neue Lebenskraft Katzenkralle – für Widerstandskraft und Wandlung Shatavari – für Weiblichkeit, Hingabe und tiefe Verbindung Kakao – für Herzöffnung und ehrliche Innenschau Mariendistel – für Schutz, Klärung und innere Wandlung Tabak – als starke symbolische Pflanze für Respekt, Verantwortung und den bewussten Umgang mit Kraft. Gerade beim Skorpion zeigt sich besonders deutlich: Transformation bedeutet nicht, alles hinter sich zu lassen. Oft geht es darum, etwas so tief zu verstehen, dass es seine Macht über uns verliert. Ob Du Skorpion bist oder nicht, diese Pflanzen können dich in der aktuellen Zeit gut unterstützen. Im neuen Blogartikel tauchen wir noch tiefer in die astrologische und traditionelle Pflanzenwelt des Skorpions ein – inklusive Mars & Pluto, Sexualität, Schattenarbeit, Regeneration und unseren passenden Dancing Shiva Blends. 👉 Den ganzen Artikel findest Du über den Link in unserer Bio. Welche dieser Pflanzen ruft dich gerade am meisten? Schreib sie in die Kommentare 🌿✨ #skorpion #sternzeichenskorpion #pflanzendersternzeichen #pflanzenastrologie #dancingshiva

candidateAudit.text: Manche Dinge brauchen einfach ihre Zeit. 🤎 Unsere Geier BIO Kruste 1902 ist genau so ein Brot. Eines, bei dem wir nichts überstürzen. Diese Kruste hat Charakter! 🤩 Kräftig gebacken, herrlich aromatisch und voller Röstaromen. Dieses Brot wird sogar doppelt in unserem Steinofen gebacken. Unsere Geier BIO Kruste 1902 kommt ganz ohne zugesetzte Hefe aus. Stattdessen geben wir unserem Natursauerteig 36 Stunden Zeit, um seinen unverwechselbaren Geschmack zu entwickeln.🌾 Außen kräftig. Innen wunderbar flauschig. 🤎 Wer unsere Geier BIO Kruste 1902 anschneidet, entdeckt eine saftige, grobporige Krume mit herrlich luftiger Struktur.🌾 Mild-säuerlich im Geschmack und voller feiner Aromen – genau so lieben wir unser Natursauerteigbrot. 😋Was kommt bei dir auf die erste Scheibe?

candidateAudit.text: 🚴 52 Teilnehmer:innen. 77.267 Kilometer. Ein starkes Team. Auf unser gemeinsames Ergebnis sind wir sehr stolz: ✅ 77.267 geradelte Kilometer ✅ 2.301.308 verbrannte Kalorien ✅ Platz 7 im Ranking bei der durchschnittlichen Kilometerleistung pro Person Zum Dank, gab es für jeden der Teilnehmenden eine kleine Anerkennung von Rauch. candidateAudit.title: Seesaibling-Ravioli mit roten Rübe sind nicht nur ein Genuss, sondern auch ein echter Hingucker am Teller. 👇 Hier geht's zum Rezept: Zutaten für 2 Personen: Teig für Ravioli: 200
candidateAudit.text: Seesaibling-Ravioli mit roten Rübe sind nicht nur ein Genuss, sondern auch ein echter Hingucker am Teller. 👇 Hier geht's zum Rezept: Zutaten für 2 Personen: Teig für Ravioli: 200 g Hartweizenmehl 1 Stk. Eier 1 EL roter Rübensaft Klarsichtfolie Füllung für Ravioli: 100 g Saiblingsfilet, geräuchert 100 g Frischkäse 1 Stk. Dotter 1 Stk. Eiweiß, verquirlt 1 EL Butter Salz und Pfeffer Zubereitung: Teig: Mehl auf Brett oder in Schüssel geben. Ei und Rübensaft hinzufügen und gut verkneten, bis ein glatter Teig daraus entsteht (bei Bedarf etwas Rübensaft bzw. Mehl hinzufügen). Aus dem Teig eine Kugel formen, in Klarsichtfolie wickeln und im Kühlschrank ca. 1/2 Stunde ruhen lassen. Füllung: Saiblingsfilet in kleine Würfel schneiden, mit Frischkäse und Dotter vermengen. Ravioli: Teig in zwei gleich große Stücke teilen und ausrollen. Eine Teighälfte in regelmäßigen Abständen mit kleinen Häufchen der Füllung belegen. Zwischenräume mit Eiweiß bestreichen. Zweite Teighälfte vorsichtig darüber legen und mit den Fingern andrücken. Ravioli ausstechen oder mit einem Teigrad ausschneiden. In kochendes Salzwasser geben, Hitze reduzieren und ca. 4 Minuten köcheln lassen. Vorsichtig herausheben, abtropfen lassen und in geschmolzener Butter schwenken. Ravioli auf Tellern anrichten und genießen. Guten Appetit! Serviervorschlag: Die Ravioli mit etwas frisch gehobeltem Parmesan abrunden.

candidateAudit.text: Damit hätten wir auch nicht gerechnet … 🌾 Seit März filmt David bei uns fast jeden Drehtag mit. Ob Licht, Kamerawinkel oder der Schnitt danach: Das meiste, was ihr hier seht, geht durch seine Hände. Als Sportler hat er seine Ernährung schon immer im Blick, Vollwert war für ihn bis dahin aber kaum ein Thema. Beim Drehen bekommt man natürlich einiges mit: wie lang ein Teig bei uns reift, was im ganzen Korn steckt, warum wir nichts wegmahlen. Irgendwann hat David dann einfach selbst ein Brot mitgenommen. Und dann noch eins. Mittlerweile kommt bei ihm zuhause kaum mehr anderes Brot auf den Tisch, und in die Jausenbox seiner Kinder auch nicht. Wer von euch hat beim Brot auch erst mit der Zeit genauer hingeschaut? #GradwohlBackstube #Vollwertbrot #Jause #BehindTheScenes #Familie

candidateAudit.title: Ihr kennt bestimmt unsere Tux-Zillertaler Rinder am Tirolerhof – aber wusstet ihr, dass die Traditionen rund um diese besondere Rasse zum Kulturerbe zählen? 🐮 Die Österreichische
candidateAudit.text: Ihr kennt bestimmt unsere Tux-Zillertaler Rinder am Tirolerhof – aber wusstet ihr, dass die Traditionen rund um diese besondere Rasse zum Kulturerbe zählen? 🐮 Die Österreichische UNESCO-Kommission hat vor wenigen Tagen das Wissen und die kulturellen Praktiken rund um das Tux-Zillertaler Rind in das Verzeichnis des immateriellen Kulturerbes aufgenommen. 📜✍️ Wir haben dieses Bestreben unterstützt. 🤎 Die Geschichte des Tux-Zillertaler Rinds und der damit verbundenen Praktiken lässt sich mindestens 200 Jahre zurückverfolgen. 🏔️ Seine kulturelle Bedeutung für die Gemeinschaft ergibt sich nicht allein aus dieser langen Geschichte und dem Erhalt der seltenen Tiroler Rinderrasse, sondern insbesondere aus der symbolischen Bedeutung der Tiere. Zu diesen zählen unter anderem die Kürung der „Moarkuh“ (Siegerkuh) 🏆 und die Überreichung einer Hahnenfeder als Siegessymbol. 🪶

candidateAudit.text: Knusper, Knusper Kekse - wir haben für euch gebacken 🍪✨ Was gibt es Schöneres in der Vorweihnachtszeit, als eine Tasse warmen Tee und richtig gute Kekse? Genau dieses wohlige Kindheitsgefühl steckt in unseren BIO Knusper Keksen Weihnachten. Das Beste daran: Sie schmecken nicht nur himmlisch nach feinen Weihnachtsgewürzen, sondern tun auch Gutes! 🍏 Für die Kekse verarbeiten wir nahrhaftes Bio-Dinkelvollkornmehl und verfeinern sie mit gerettetem Apfelpüree aus niederösterreichischer Landwirtschaft. So wird aus wertvollem Obst knuspriger Weihnachtsgenuss statt Lebensmittelverschwendung. Unser Genuss-Tipp: Perfekt zum Knabbern für zwischendurch, als kleines, nachhaltiges Mitbringsel für eure Liebsten oder grob zerbröselt als winterliches Schichtdessert im Glas! candidateAudit.text: Die Geheimzutat in diesem veganen Schokomousse? Schwarze Bohnen. 🫘 Klingt spannend? Schmeckt unglaublich! Probiert es unbedingt aus ✨ VEGANES SCHOKOMOUSSE (2 Portionen) Zutaten: 150 g Schokolade (Zartbitter) 240 g schwarze Bohnen, gekocht 125 ml Mandeldrink (Milchalternative nach Wahl) 1 EL MANI Bläuel natives Olivenöl extra, Selection optional: Etwas Zimt & Ahornsirup Zubereitung: Milch in einem Topf erwärmen und die Schokolade darin langsam schmelzen. Zusammen mit den Bohnen, Olivenöl und Zimt (optional) in einem Blender mixen, bis ein cremiges Mousse entsteht. Abschmecken und nach Bedarf einen Schuss Ahornsirup hinzufügen. In Dessertschalen füllen und mindestens 30 Minuten im Kühlschrank kaltstellen. Zum Servieren mit etwas Olivenöl und Meersalzflocken verfeinern. #schokomousse #veganesschokomousse #schokoladeundolivenöl #manibläuel #bioolivenöl

candidateAudit.title: Ein Stück Heimat auf dem Jausentisch. 🤎 Es gibt Brote, die wecken Erinnerungen. An gemeinsame Jausen, an den Duft von frisch geschnittenem Brot und an die Küche bei den Großeltern
candidateAudit.text: Ein Stück Heimat auf dem Jausentisch. 🤎 Es gibt Brote, die wecken Erinnerungen. An gemeinsame Jausen, an den Duft von frisch geschnittenem Brot und an die Küche bei den Großeltern. Unser Weinviertler Landbrot steht für genau diese vertrauten Genussmomente. Ein klassisches Roggenmischbrot, das unsere Verbundenheit mit dem Weinviertel widerspiegelt. Welchen Kindheitsmoment verbindest du mit frischem Brot? 🍞 #sourdough #sourdoughbread #sauerteig #sauerteigbrot Tradition, die man nicht nur sieht, sondern schmeckt. 🌾 Unser Weinviertler Landbrot ist ein Stück österreichische Brotkultur. Mit BIO Natursauerteig und 18 Stunden Teigreife entsteht ein Brot mit ursprünglichem Charakter und angenehm mild-säuerlichem Geschmack. Hast du unser Weinviertler Landbrot schon verkostet? Manchmal ist die einfachste Jause die beste. 🧈🌱 Eine Scheibe Weinviertler Landbrot, etwas Butter und frisch geschnittener Schnittlauch. Mehr braucht es oft gar nicht, um sich ein Stück Heimat auf den Teller zu holen. Sein aromatischer, mild-säuerlicher Geschmack macht unser Landbrot zum idealen Begleiter für eine traditionelle Jause.

candidateAudit.title: What are the terms under which media acts through lore, noise, sense, and air? With its second edition of the ’In Terms of Media…’ symposium the Weibel Institute for Digital Cultur
candidateAudit.text: What are the terms under which media acts through lore, noise, sense, and air? With its second edition of the ’In Terms of Media…’ symposium the Weibel Institute for Digital Culture continues it's ongoing engagement with contemporary media technologies. weibel.institute Across four panels and one workshop, the symposium brings together artists, theorists, and practitioners to trace these registers from multiple angles, attending to the historical conditions from which our present has emerged and the alternative practices it might yet generate. 5 Nov 15:00–16:30 Lore With Günseli Yalcinkaya, Valentina Tanni, Gary Zhexi Zhang. Moderation: Sophie Publig 17:00–18:30 Noise With Sonia de Jager, Miguel Prado Casanova, Patricia Reed. Moderation: Mikkel Rørbo 6 Nov 15:00–16:30 Sense With Elisa Balmaceda, Josephine Berry, Aura Satz. Moderation: Denise Helene Sumi 17:00–18:30 Air With Anna Engelhardt, Jamieson Webster. Moderation: Asia Bazdyrieva 19:00–22:00 Unwind with DJ Set by Inou Ki Endo and Live Set by Nzumbe inoukiendo miguelprad0 — AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse 2 / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna ail.angewandte.at — Additional program (not at AIL): 4 Nov, 10:00–16:00 at Weibel Institute for Digital Cultures, Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna Futures of the Self Workshop with Jesse Damiani Please register for the workshop via this mail to: weibel.institute@uni-ak.ac.at (Unfortunately, the planned screening at the MUMOK had to be cancelled.)

candidateAudit.text: Frag Adi: WTF is Garam Masala? 🌶️ In unserer neuen Serie „Frag Adi“ geht’s um indische Küche kurz, ehrlich und ohne Mythen. #indiancuisinedemystified Folge 1: Garam Masala heißt übersetzt „warme Gewürzmischung“. 🔥 Unbedingt zum Schluss ins Curry geben. So bleiben die Aromen besonders gut erhalten und geben dem Gericht den richtigen Kick. Das eine Garam Masala? Gibt’s nicht. Die Mischung variiert je nach Region und Familie. In unserem Mama Masala nach altem Familienrezept ist Kreuzkümmel, Anis, Bockshornkleesamen, Nelken, Koriander, Pfeffer, Zimt, Ingwer, Kümmel und Knoblauch. 🫙 In der nächsten Folge: Was unterscheidet Garam Masala eigentlich von Currypulver? 👀 Was wollt ihr sonst über indische Küche wissen? Fragen ab in die Kommentare! 👇 #fragadi #garammasala #indischkochen #gewürze indianfood wienessen karmafood

candidateAudit.text: Weiter geht’s mit unserer Reihe “Unsere ProduzentInnen”! Heute führt uns die Reise nach Italien: Corilu ist eine Kooperative, zu der sich 1998 Haselnussbauern aus Lu Monferrato in der Provinz Alessandria zusammengeschlossen haben. In der sanften Hügellandschaft des Piemont gedeihen die edlen Nüsse unter idealen klimatischen Bedingungen. Die Bauern sind seit Generationen in dieser Region verwurzelt und haben sich das Ziel gesetzt, die seit dem 16. Jahrhundert bestehende Tradition des Haselnussanbaus im Piemont in kleinbäuerlicher Tradition nachhaltig zu sichern. Wischt durch die Bilder und lernt Corilu kennen! In unserem Online-Shop und unserer Greißlerei bieten wir die gerösteten Haselnüsse sowie die Haselnusscreme der Marke Corilu an! #krusteundkrume #corilu #piemonte

candidateAudit.text: TONIGHT! MAD FELLAZ Only 15€ (Explore New Artist Ticket) Mad Fellaz is an eclectic progressive band founded in 2011 by guitarist and primary composer Paolo Busatto in Bassano del Grappa (Italy). Initially inspired by the legendary artists of classic progressive rock, the band has continually evolved with outstanding versatility and creativity—both in instrumental and vocal music. Their compositions draw influence from the great prog giants such as King Crimson, Genesis, Gentle Giant, and Yes, while also embracing the innovation of more recent artists like Snarky Puppy, Screaming Headless Torsos, Vulfpeck, and beyond—without limiting themselves to any specific genre. Currently composed of eight musicians, Mad Fellaz features members who have studied, collaborated, or recorded with prominent names such as Chick Corea Elektric Band, Dave Weckl, Gary Meek, Peter Erskine, Zucchero, Stan Sargeant, Fabio Trentini (Guano Apes, Le Orme), William Dotto (Le Orme, Banco del Mutuo Soccorso), John Etheridge (Soft Machine), Jim Mullen. Their most recent album, „Road To Planet Circus“ (February 2022, produced by Fabio Trentini), marks a pivotal moment in the band’s musical evolution. Embracing a more groove-oriented direction, the record features a rich blend of Jazz-Rock, Fusion, Funk, and Afrobeat, in compositions where each instrument is celebrated for its unique timbral identity. They are currently recording two new albums. One is a progressive fusion album, and the other will be very eclectic and varied.

candidateAudit.text: Okay, okay, ich komme darauf gerade wirklich nicht klar. Aber ich möchte dieses Video einfach genau so hier posten. Ohne Musik, ohne großen Tam-Tam, ohne irgendetwas daran zu verändern. Einfach dieser Moment, genau so, wie er passiert ist. Weil ich ihn auf meinem Profil haben möchte. Als Erinnerung an einen Moment, den ich mir so oft gewünscht habe. 🥹 Es gibt nämlich auch genügend Momente, in denen ich mich frage: Warum mache ich das alles? Warum investiere ich so viel Zeit, Energie und Herzblut in meinen Content? Und manchmal fühlen sich diese großen Brands einfach so unerreichbar an. Und dann gibt es Momente wie diesen. In denen ich plötzlich ein exklusives pradabeauty PR-Paket auspacke und mir einfach nur denke: Serap, dein Content wird gesehen. 🥹 Egal, wie klein du bist. Egal, wie langsam du wächst. Es gibt Brands, die deine organische Reichweite, deine Kreativität und die Qualität deiner Arbeit sehen und schätzen. Ich habe so oft solche exklusiven PR-Pakete bei anderen Creatorn gesehen und mir gedacht: Oh mein Gott, wie cool wäre es, irgendwann auch einmal so etwas erleben zu dürfen. Und jetzt sitze ich hier und habe es tatsächlich selbst bekommen. Damit habe ich wirklich überhaupt nicht gerechnet. Ich glaube, das Video zeigt sowieso viel mehr, als ich jemals in Worte fassen könnte. Ich wollte diese Freude einfach mit euch teilen und diesen Moment hier festhalten. ❤️ Und an alle Mädels da draußen: Traut euch. Macht es einfach. Scheißt auf die Meinung anderer und lasst euch nicht entmutigen, nur weil ihr vielleicht noch nicht dort seid, wo ihr gerne wärt. Jeder einzel

candidateAudit.text: BOOM TSCHAK! 💥 20 Jahre dorisuhlich: Das tanzquartierwien feiert die Choreografin mit einem großen Festival aus Performances, Tanz, Sound und Workshops. Von frühen Arbeiten bis zu ihren bekanntesten Produktionen zeigt das Festival zwei Jahrzehnte künstlerisches Schaffen und ihre Auseinandersetzung mit Körper, Bewegung und gesellschaftlichen Normen. 💥 BOOM TSCHAK: 20 Jahre Doris Uhlich 🗓️ 05.11. bis 05.12. 🎟️ Tickets erhältlich im MQ Point oder Onlineshop 🔴 #MuseumsQuartier #TanzquartierWien #DorisUhlich BOOM TSCHAK! 💥 20 years of dorisuhlich: tanzquartierwien celebrates the choreographer with a major festival featuring performances, dance, sound and workshops. candidateAudit.title: Inside the exhibition 03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis. The climate crisis is our omni-present companion these days, why not take it o
candidateAudit.text: Inside the exhibition 03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis. The climate crisis is our omni-present companion these days, why not take it on a walk? Inspired by the deconstruction of soil caused by drought, the work ‘chainmail’ was made to make the literal weight of climate change on our shoulders something we can physically experience. This ‘fashion’ piece is meant to be worn throughout the visit of this ­exhibition, inviting the visitors to reflect on their own actions and feelings concerning the climate crisis: What is my purpose in this? How do I work through my feelings? What makes me feel better? What can I do to make the world a better place? At the end of the visit, the weight is taken off as a ­symbolic act of katharsis. Contribution by: Johanna Unterpertinger At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna running till 6 Nov 2026 Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 Photos: Hannah Mayr

candidateAudit.text: What if your favourite flat white could taste surprisingly different? Same milk. Same recipe. Same barista. Just different coffee beans. One coffee might bring out notes of chocolate, nuts and caramel. Another might be brighter, fruitier or more floral. Even with milk, those differences can come through. That’s one of the things we love about specialty coffee — there’s always something new to discover, even in the drink you order every day. At Loka, we always have two espresso options in our grinders, each with a distinct flavour profile. So next time you’re here, ask our baristas about the options and try your usual drink with something new. And if you prefer decaf, we’ve got you covered too! We’re always happy to make your favourite drink with decaf espresso — just let our baristas know. You might just find a new favourite 🤍

candidateAudit.title: MINA, OUR NEW TEAM MEMBER AT MAISON NAYA Please join us to welcome MINA. Mina was born and raised in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. She was a bright second-year medical student studying ge
candidateAudit.text: MINA, OUR NEW TEAM MEMBER AT MAISON NAYA Please join us to welcome MINA. Mina was born and raised in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia. She was a bright second-year medical student studying general medicine at a local university. She hoped to become a surgeon. She had 3 more years to finish her degree followed by 2 years of hospital practice and 3 more years of specialized study. So, 8 more years ahead to become a surgeon. During her studies, she worked in a specialty coffee shop for many years. She realised she had fallen more in love with café culture and coffee beans than a surgeon's knife. Behind her soft demeanor and sweet smile lies a brave, adventurous, and decisive woman. Mina decided the world was too big to spend another 8 years stuck in Mongolia. She wanted to see other parts of the world. Since she had already learned German as a foreign language, why not move to a German-speaking country? And here we are. She arrived in Vienna. Her first time living abroad and likely the first time she has felt truly alive and motivated. She is now studying German at an advanced level to prepare for the University of Vienna, where she plans to study business. Mina used to be our regular customer who loved our team's vibe, so she applied for a job with us. We felt her strength and positive energy during the interview plus her very good barista skills, we happily welcomed her into our place. Now VlENNA is her new home and MAlSON NAYA is her new family. (to be honest, we feel super safe working with someone who knows First Aid by heart) Come by to say hi to Mina sometime! 🩵 #maisonnayavienna

candidateAudit.text: Der Chef einer Bäckerei wählt Pizza. Zufall? Wohl kaum. 🍕 Wer bei uns nach Pizza sucht, wird nämlich fündig: Unser Pizzaweckerl ist quasi die Backstubenversion davon. Der Unterschied liegt vorallem im Teig: Wir backen ihn mit Vollkorn, das gibt mehr Biss, ein nussigeres Aroma und macht ihn nährstoff- und ballaststoffreich. Das Schnitzel, die wahre Liebe aller Österreicher, verkaufen wir leider nicht. Ganz ohne Bäcker kommt aber auch das nicht aus: Die Panier entsteht traditionell aus Semmelbröseln, also aus getrocknetem Gebäck. Ohne uns wär das Schnitzel streng genommen nackt. 😄 Und wenn ihr euch nur mehr für ein einziges Essen entscheiden müsstet: Was wäre es? #GradwohlBackstube #Pizzaweckerl #Lieblingsessen #Backwissen #Team

candidateAudit.text: Save the date! Next exhibition opening is coming up: 18 Nov, 18:00 With contributions by: adO/Aptive, Beatrice Tulagan, Eline Benjaminsen, Elias Kimaiyo, Forensic Architecture, Jonas Staal, Paolo Cirio, Prin Rodriguez, Radha D’Souza, Valentino Skarwan The engagement with climate justice reveals a complex field of perspectives across multiple temporalities, geographies, and forms of knowledge. In this context, environmental destruction is entangled with economic interests, the uneven distribution of risks and responsibilities, colonial continuities, imperialist power relations, and geological deep time. The exhibition ’Future on Trial. Between Unruly Evidence and Unfinished Climate Justice’ moves between two conceptions of justice. One that is produced and negotiated in courtrooms through scientific and legal evidence, data, and visual investigations, and another that understands justice as an unfinished, collective process, grounded in Indigenous knowledge, queer ecology, multispecies perspectives, and activism. Through a dialogue between artistic practices and scientific experts in the field of climate litigation, the exhibition opens up a space between evidence and uncertainty, accusation and repair, institutional accountability and collective imagination. candidateAudit.title: Inside the exhibition 03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis. Mainly painted with self-made colours from soil and plant pigments, ‘Entangled
candidateAudit.text: Inside the exhibition 03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis. Mainly painted with self-made colours from soil and plant pigments, ‘Entangled’ pictures an underground view of root and ­mycelium structures. Inspired by minirhizotrones (scientific instruments to observe roots and their interactions with soil, mycelium and microorganisms over time), it offers an immersive experience of the hidden world beneath our feet while emphasising our profound connection with soil as the foundation of life, providing nutrients and supporting ecosystems. By inviting us to reflect on the entanglement of healthy soil and human well being in times of severe drought caused by human-made climate change, it opens a deeper understanding of us being part of more-than-human nature. The work ’Veins’ is inspired by the colorful digital maps of Root Image Analysis Software, which scientists use to trace and examine root networks from minirhizotron imagery. The embroidery of roots in red colour intentionally mirrors human vascular systems. This visual bridge shows the deep relation of human bodies and soil bodies, and reminds us that our survival and wellbeing is ­directly connected to healthy soil. The delicate chiffon acts as a metaphor for the fragile threshold between the above-ground world and the underground ecosystem. Referring to ‘Entangled’, ‘Veins’ steps into the lens of digital root scans – transforming scientific data into a poetic testament of more-than-human entanglements. candidateAudit.text: Next round of AIL Ping-Pong – an intervention at Counter 13 with Christos Kyritopoulos-Ninas, Florian Sorgo, Felix Helmut Wagner, Agnes Varnai In its fourth edition, AIL Ping-Pong circles around the term and meaning of ‘blob.’ In Computer Science and Technology BLOB stands for a ‘Binary Large Object’ and is a collection of raw binary data stored as a single object. In biology, the term blob refers to a specific type of fungus consisting of a single, enormous cell. It has no brain, yet it can still learn, solve problems, and move. A blob is a form without fixed contours. It defies clear categorization: it grows, melts, merges, engulfs, and mutates. Something between body and mass, organism and data packet, slime trail and digital artifact. It can appear soft and funny – or threatening, viral, uncontrollable. Presented in the small vitrine of the Otto Wagner Postsparkasse, four graduates of the University of Applied Arts Vienna open a window into their diverse artistic practices, offering a range of perspectives that explore parallels, contrasts, or extensions within the given thematic framework AIL, Otto Wagner Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna agnes_varnai felixhelmutwagner chris_ckrtn flo_vago Photo: Agnes Varnai

candidateAudit.text: Ready to turn your practice upside down? Join Vasiliki for a playful, focused 2-hour Rocket Yoga masterclass dedicated to inversions, arm balances and the art of finding balance off the ground. Through a dynamic Rocket flow, technical breakdowns and smart drills, we’ll explore how strength, alignment and breath work together to build stability, confidence and ease in challenging poses. What to expect? ✨ A warm-up for the wrists, shoulders and core to protect the joints and build a strong foundation. ✨ A dynamic Rocket flow to build heat and strength, including floats and jump-throughs. ✨ Step-by-step exploration of arm balances, including Crow Pose (Bakasana) and Side Crow (Parsva Bakasana). ✨ Inversion practice — from Tripod and Sirsasana headstands to forearm stands and handstand drills at the wall. ✨ Playful transitions, including Crow to Headstand. Whether you’re taking your first flight or refining poses you already know, you’ll have space to explore each posture at your own pace, challenge yourself and have fun along the way. No previous inversion experience needed — just a regular Vinyasa practice, curiosity and a willingness to try (and fall!) again. 📌 Rocket Yoga Masterclass: Inversions & Arm Balances with yuj_vasiliki 📌 Saturday, November 28 | 11:00–13:00 Booking via Eversports 🤍 📷 giannis_skarlatos_

candidateAudit.text: Inside the exhibition 03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis. ’The Experiment’ is both deconstruction and reconstruction of a field experiment run by researchers at the University of Innsbruck, which simulates summer drought in a mountain grassland. Open for visitors to enter, the installation dismantles scientific processes and transforms a fictitious laboratory setting into an immersive environment, where the material traces of experimentation and data collection can be engaged with. The observer – both inside and outside of the­ ­transparent sheltered space – is invited to reflect on the nature of exploration, (drought) memory and the construction of reality. Contribution by: Michael Bahn, Konstantina Maria Serjannis At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna running till 6 Nov 2026 Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 Photos: Hannah Mayr

candidateAudit.text: Please note: Symposium starts already at 15:00✌️What are the terms under which media acts through lore, noise, sense, and air? With its second instalment, the ‘In Terms of Media…’ symposium continues the Weibel Institute for Digital Culture's ongoing engagement with contemporary media technologies. Our present is shaped not only by visible architectures of data and computation, but also by registers that precede or exceed explicit discourse: 🧶 the mythological and occult substrates through which technological imaginaries take hold; 🧶 the noise from which systems, meanings, and exclusions emerge; 🧶 the conditions of mediated life and their entanglement with colonial histories of power and sensing; 🧶 the atmospheric environments that orient conduct and produce consent without explicit command. Across four panels and one workshop, the symposium brings together artists, theorists, and practitioners to trace these registers from multiple angles, attending to the historical conditions from which our present has emerged and the alternative practices it might yet generate. With: Elisa Balmaceda, Josephine Berry, Anna Engelhardt, Sonia de Jager, Miguel Prado Casanova, Patricia Reed, Aura Satz, Valentina Tanni, Jamieson Webster, Günseli Yalcinkaya, Gary Zhexi Zhang, and Jesse Damiani Presented by The Weibel Institute for Digital Cultures. The symposium will be held in English

candidateAudit.text: Ever wondered why the same coffee can taste so different depending on how it’s brewed? At Loka, there’s more than one way to enjoy a good cup — from the intensity of espresso to the delicate complexity of V60 and the smooth, refreshing character of cold brew. Swipe through to discover what makes each brewing method different ➡️ The way you brew coffee can completely change how it tastes — even when you’re using the same beans. None of these methods is necessarily better than the others. They simply reveal different sides of coffee, depending on what you enjoy and what you’re in the mood for. And if V60 has sparked your curiosity, keep an eye on our next announcement. We have something brewing for you 🤍 ESPRESSO Small, concentrated, and full of character. Brewed under pressure, espresso delivers an intense flavour and a rich body — whether enjoyed on its own or as the base of your favourite milk drink. V60 A slower, more hands-on way of brewing. Hot water is poured over freshly ground coffee through a paper filter, creating a clean, delicate cup where subtle fruity, floral, and other flavour notes have room to shine. COLD BREW Coffee brewed with cold water over several hours. The result? A smooth, refreshing drink, often with natural sweetness and less perceived bitterness.

candidateAudit.text: Inside the exhibition 03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis. Three transparent cylinders reveal the hidden layers of soil as it is exposed to increasing levels of dryness. As experimental drought progresses over the course of the exhibition, the structure and appearance of the soil changes. Visible traces like cracks, compaction, and disintegration reflect the gradient of water supply and –scarcity in the three vessels. The installation Drought Traces points to the fragile balance between water, soil and life. Drought Traces. Contribution by: Michael Bahn, Cornelia Dirnberger, Christian Prohammer At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. candidateAudit.text: Seit 260 Jahren erhalten und pflegen die Praterbetreiber*innen die Tradition, die Kultur und die einzigartige Atmosphäre des Wurstelpraters – und nun ist es soweit: Die Österreichische UNESCO-Kommission nimmt die Wiener Wurstelpraterkultur in das Nationale Verzeichnis des Immateriellen Kulturerbes auf! ✨🎡😊 Am Montag, 19. Oktober 2026 lädt der Wiener Praterverband anlässlich der Anerkennung zum Immateriellen Kulturerbe zur Pressekonferenz mit Silvia Lang (Präsidentin des Praterverbands), Elisabeth Zehetner (Tourismus-Staatssekretärin), Veronica Kaup-Hasler (Stadträtin für Kultur und Wissenschaft), Alexander Nikolai (Bezirksvorsteher Leopoldstadt). 📅 Mo, 19. Oktober 2026 ⏰ 9:30 🗺️ Pratermuseum Was ist die Wiener Wurstelpraterkultur? 🔍🤔😊 Wie der Name schon vermuten lässt, geht es dabei ausdrücklich nicht um den Wurstelprater als Ort, sondern um das Wissen rund um die im Wurstelprater gepflegte Kultur des Vergnügens. Seit 1766 wird sie von Generation zu Generation weitergegeben und hoch gehalten. Neben dem ungewöhnlichen und besonderen Leben der Praterbetreiber*innen, spielt auch die gesellschaftliche Bedeutung eine große Rolle - die Wurstelpraterkultur ermöglicht und lebt seit jeher die Begegnung von Menschen aller Herkunft und allen Alters 🫶 #wurstelprater #unescokulturerbe #prater #wurstelpraterkultur #wien

candidateAudit.title: Inside the exhibition 03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis. Hands touch, intervene, secure traces, expose. Cutting, tearing, rubbing. Soil
candidateAudit.text: Inside the exhibition 03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis. Hands touch, intervene, secure traces, expose. Cutting, tearing, rubbing. Soil is both experimental surface and site of action. Distance between body and ground, the disposable latex glove as a separating membrane. As a symbol of experiment and intervention, the glove marks the moment of active intervention; the motif evokes experimental setups in the field, laboratory situations in situ, and, at the same time, forensic investigation. Through exposing, drilling, and excavating, the ground becomes a site of ambivalent human-environment relations: between proximity and separation, intervention and restraint. The Tat-Ort is a locus of forensic ethnography, where observation and analysis intersect with remnants of violation and evidence collection. The installation assembles fragments of an artistic research process – notes, materials, objects, traces – on soil and drought. On the table, the act of investigation becomes visible: the laboratory table transforms into both a site of knowledge production and a scene of evidence. [Exhibit B] hands on – hands off [Exhibit A] Am Tat-Ort: ­Evidence on the Laboratory Table Contributions by: Konstantina Maria Serjannis At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. candidateAudit.text: Save the date and register for this workshop 🌐 We live in a highly globalised and hyper-connected world. At the same time, it feels like falling apart: To a large extent, we have lost connection – to ‘others’ in society, to ‘other’ kinds of knowing, and to something we are used to call ‘nature’. What really matters to us? Is it possible to un-learn and un-do ingrained habits or routines resulting in ways of living severely threatening ecosystems and resulting in multiple socio-ecological crises we are facing nowadays? Out of a sense of urgency, can a mindset emerge that entails a more-than-human way of thinking and acting, both individually and collectively? Workshop with Franziska Allerberger. Duration: 13:15–15:30 Please register for this workshop via link in bio! (free entry) The workshop is an invitation to explore these questions and themes by getting in motion through a performative and embodied approach. In doing so, we also reflect upon the creative potential of art-science collaborations (such as 03: Soil) for unleashing societal change towards a healthier future on Planet Earth. Franziska Allerberger is a geographer and pursues a training in theater pedagogy. She is interested in interfaces of science, arts, policy and civil society, and how collaborations between these distinct actor groups can be facilitated and strengthened to contribute to a livable future. Her geographic perspective is the starting point for her artistic explorations at AIL. Part of the exhibition ‘03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’

candidateAudit.text: Come join the next Soil Session this Thursday, 17:00. You are invited to participate in the multi-channel sound installation Soil Immersion by Christian Prohammer and Johanna Unterpertinger. Following three recording sessions during the runtime of our current exhibition, your voice and sound fragments are integrated into the immersive layering of sound. Come early and catch the next exhibition tour too: starting 16:00. (Free entry, no registration) AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna About the exhibition: 03: Soil Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis Soil is a highly diverse and sensitive cosmos that is facing increasing pressure due to the climate crisis, as a result of more frequent and severe extreme events such as drought. Soil holds histories, stories and belowground storage systems, repositories of information and traces of past worlds, current developments and future scenarios. The exhibition emerges from the project 03: Soil, which is based on interdisciplinary and site-specific artistic research, and is rooted in a collective field exploration of a subalpine ecological research laboratory in the Stubai Valley (Tyrol, Austria). At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. This creates a dialogue at the intersection of data collection, scientific exploration and artistic translation, in which soil becomes a ground for research, creativity, evidence and metaphors. candidateAudit.text: Thanks for joining the opening of the exhibition ‘03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’ this week! At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. This creates a dialogue at the intersection of data collection, scientific exploration and artistic translation, in which soil becomes a ground for research, creativity, evidence and metaphor. — on till 5 Nov 2026 Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 The exhibition emerges from the project 03: Soil, which is based on interdisciplinary and site-specific artistic research, and is rooted in a collective field exploration of a subalpine ecological research laboratory in the Stubai Valley (Tyrol, Austria). candidateAudit.title: There’s no single way we want coffee at Loka to taste. Sometimes we’re looking for balance and sweetness. Sometimes for bright fruit and acidity. And sometimes for something a litt
candidateAudit.text: There’s no single way we want coffee at Loka to taste. Sometimes we’re looking for balance and sweetness. Sometimes for bright fruit and acidity. And sometimes for something a little more unexpected. That’s why we currently work with three specialty roasters — thebarnberlin, kaffeelix.roastery and dakcoffeeroasters — each bringing a very different character to our coffee bar. From smooth, chocolatey espresso to bright, fruit-driven coffees and more playful, unexpected flavour profiles — together they give us room to explore just how different coffee can taste. Swipe through to meet the three roasters behind our coffee — and what we love about each of them 🤍 THE BARN · BERLIN A pioneer of European specialty coffee, THE BARN is known for beautifully roasted coffees with a naturally sweet, smooth character. At Loka, it’s our choice for a more classic espresso profile — think chocolate, nuts, balance and sweetness. KAFFEELIX · ST. PÖLTEN World-class roasting, close to home. Led by World Coffee Roasting Champion Felix Teiretzbacher, KAFFELIX brings a brighter side of coffee to our bar — lively acidity, beautiful fruit notes and plenty of character. DAK · AMSTERDAM DAK takes specialty coffee beyond the expected, combining light roasting with playful processing and complex, fruit-driven flavour profiles. The one to try when you’re curious to discover just how surprising coffee can be.

candidateAudit.title: Artificial intelligence is often framed as a quest to replicate the human brain, promising frictionless cognition and a future of seamless automation. But what if this pervasive na
candidateAudit.text: Artificial intelligence is often framed as a quest to replicate the human brain, promising frictionless cognition and a future of seamless automation. But what if this pervasive narrative obscures a deeper, more ‘errant’ truth? Media theorist and author Clemens Apprich in conversation with philosopher Jan Völker. Moderated by Amanda Holmes, Department of Philosophy, University of Applied Arts Vienna Welcome: Ulrike Kuch, Rector of the University of Applied Arts Vienna A cooperation of the department of Media Theory and the department of Philosophy. ‘Errant Intelligence’ challenges the prevailing biological and individualistic interpretations of machine learning, arguing instead for a radical understanding of machine intelligence. The book embraces the deviations, inconsistencies, and ‘errant behaviour’ as fundamental to the discovery of new knowledge, moving beyond the illusion of mere optimisation. Drawing on media theory, cybernetics, and a unique psychoanalytic lens, it explores the ‘technological unconscious’ of machine learning. It traces the historical roots of AI, from early automatons and the Turing machine to natural language processing and contemporary machine learning systems. Challenging the idea of an autonomous, self-generating AI, the book exposes the hidden labour, assumed logics, and inherent biases that animate its operation. It re-evaluates computational thinking, insisting on its inherently social, collective, and symbolic character, and revealing how language and logical paradoxes are not obstacles but constitutive forces that shape intelligent machines

candidateAudit.text: In this workshop with Helena Detsch we will explore simple ways to create a fascinating natural color palette from soil and plant-based materials like earths, minerals, vegetables, kitchen supplies and algae pigments. Part of the exhibition ‘03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’ Duration: 15:30–17:30 Please register for this workshop via link in bio (free entry) Together, we'll first experiment with making self-made oil- or watercolors from 100% natural sources and then explore the many possibilities of sustainable painting, discovering how these self-made colors behave on paper and fabric and what a truly organic painting practice can look like. In her oil paintings, installations and animations, Helena Detsch explores (mis-)relationships between humans and more-than-human life. Her series and immersive spatial installations question Western anthropocentric narratives about nature as a resource and create spaces to reflect on coexistence and complex interconnections between human and other agents. To develop a more sustainable art practice, she crafts natural colors from plant and soil pigments. helena.kettu AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna dieangewandte

candidateAudit.text: About the next exhibition at AIL: Soil is a highly diverse and sensitive cosmos that is facing increasing pressure due to the climate crisis, as a result of more frequent and severe extreme events such as drought. Soil holds histories, stories and belowground storage systems, repositories of information and traces of past worlds, current developments and future scenarios. What is happening beneath our feet? At AIL researchers and artists show their open, collaborative process, which unfolds in a multiperspective inquiry on soil and drought. This creates a dialogue at the intersection of data collection, scientific exploration and artistic translation, in which soil becomes a ground for research, creativity, evidence and metaphors. With contributions by: Franziska Allerberger (Geographer), Michael Bahn (Ecologist), Helena Detsch (Visual Artist), Cornelia Dirnberger (Visual Artist), Christian Prohammer (Musician, Audio Engineer), Nora Schöpfer (Visual Artist), Konstantina Maria Serjannis (Cultural Scientist), Johanna Unterpertinger (Musician) ’03: Soil. Between (De-)Composition and (Re-)Construction in the Climate Crisis’ emerges from the project 03: Soil, which is based on interdisciplinary and site-specific artistic research, and is rooted in a collective field exploration of a subalpine ecological research laboratory in the Stubai Valley (Tyrol, Austria). candidateAudit.title: Why doesn’t all coffee taste like… coffee? If you’ve ever had a cup that tasted surprisingly fruity, floral, chocolatey or sweet, there’s a reason for it. Where coffee is grown, ho
candidateAudit.text: Why doesn’t all coffee taste like… coffee? If you’ve ever had a cup that tasted surprisingly fruity, floral, chocolatey or sweet, there’s a reason for it. Where coffee is grown, how it’s processed, roasted and finally brewed — all of these things shape what eventually ends up in your cup. This idea is at the heart of third-wave coffee: treating coffee less like a commodity and more like a product with its own origin, character and flavour. It brought more attention to where coffee comes from, single-origin beans, careful brewing and lighter roasting — allowing the natural fruity, floral and other distinctive notes of the beans to come through rather than being dominated by the roast itself. It’s also what shapes the coffee we choose at Loka. We work with specialty roasters and look for coffees with a distinct origin and character — coffees that have something of their own to say in the cup. Over the next few weeks, our Coffee Series will take a closer look at the roasters we work with, the coffees on our bar, and the different ways to brew and experience them. Because good coffee should taste like where it came from — not just like coffee 🤍

candidateAudit.text: One of the highlights of Tatiana Koshkarova’s upcoming visit to Loka will be a workshop dedicated entirely to the art of hands-on assisting. A thoughtful hands-on assist is not simply about taking a practitioner deeper into a pose. Offered with knowledge, sensitivity and clear intention, it can create greater stability or space, help someone experience an asana differently, and deepen their understanding of the practice. Hands-on assisting is one of the defining features of the Jivamukti Yoga method — and one of the areas Tatiana Koshkarova is particularly known for within the Jivamukti community. Her approach is rooted in years of practice, teaching and teacher education. During this 3-hour workshop, Tatiana will share this accumulated experience through clear explanations and demonstrations, different approaches to assisting, and plenty of hands-on practice in pairs. The workshop is especially relevant for yoga teachers and those preparing for teacher training, but is equally open to dedicated practitioners who want to deepen their understanding of assisting and asana. 📌 The Art of Assisting with tatianakoshkarova October 10 • 13:00–16:00 Booking via Eversports — link in bio 🤍

candidateAudit.text: ✨ SAVE THE DATE: 7–11 October 2026 ✨ This October, we’re excited to welcome a special guest teacher to Loka — tatianakoshkarova, an 800-hour certified Advanced Jivamukti Yoga Teacher with extensive experience teaching classes, workshops and continuing education for yoga teachers around the world (Barcelona, Paris, Berlin, Vienna, Lisbon and Dubai). Tatiana mentors teachers through the Jivamukti Teacher Apprenticeship Program (JTAP), has served multiple times as a mentor on Jivamukti 75-hour trainings, and has participated in Advanced Board examinations in Paris, Berlin and Rome. In 2027, she will also be a mentor at the 300-hour Jivamukti Yoga Teacher Training in India. Her classes combine thoughtfully structured asana sequences with breathwork, meditation, yogic teachings, music and intention. She is also particularly known within the Jivamukti community for her expertise in hands-on assisting. candidateAudit.title: Coming up next as part of VIENNA DESIGN WEEK 2026 🪢 The exhibition ’Zero and One Chairs’ was created as part of MATCH!, a recurring initiative organised by the department of Appli
candidateAudit.text: Coming up next as part of VIENNA DESIGN WEEK 2026 🪢 The exhibition ’Zero and One Chairs’ was created as part of MATCH!, a recurring initiative organised by the department of Applied Photography and Time-Based Media at the University of Applied Arts Vienna, which explores the synergistic potential of student teams from different degree programs. In collaboration with the department Industrial Design, this year’s focus was on the intersection of photography and the object, with particular attention paid to the relationship with set design, styling, casting and narrative. Seen from the perspective of Applied Photography, the object and thus the chair, is a welcome protagonist. Photography’s multiple applied genres are cited here: documentary, fashion, advertising, architecture and the portrait. When the function in Industrial Design coalesces with the idea of the purpose in Applied Photography, the question of factuality emerges. Be not mistaken: The most literal things are often the most confusing and enigmatic. Between what it is and how it is*, worlds unfold. We put the images to work. VDW Cocktail: 29 Sep, 17:00–18:00 Showcase and drinks followed by a collective walk to the billboards in front of the main entrance of the University Open Saturdays: 26 Sep / 3 Oct, 11:00–18:00 Opening hours: Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna The collaborative works are on display at the AIL and on the billboards at the university’s main entrance on Oskar-Kokoschka-Platz. dieangewandte viennadesignweek applied.photography angewandte_id Feat

candidateAudit.title: OMHU TEDDY SOFA DAY Three months ago, we were looking for a sofa for our living room setup at MAISON NAYA. Naya and Tabea searched everywhere--both online and in furniture shops ar
candidateAudit.text: OMHU TEDDY SOFA DAY Three months ago, we were looking for a sofa for our living room setup at MAISON NAYA. Naya and Tabea searched everywhere--both online and in furniture shops around Vienna but unfortunately our budget was very tight since we are a small, just-starting café business. So, we decided to wait. Then one ordinary morning, We checked our email inbox. We saw an extraordinary email from OMHU Copenhagen omhu_cph They told us they wanted to send us a gift: an ORIGINAL TEDDY SOFA! Wait... what? Naya and Tabea weren't sure if they were reading it correctly and reread the email several times. Next came a phone call between Vienna and Copenhagen. The OMHU representative was so sweet and kind. They told us they had noticed us, perhaps they came across our Instagram? Imagine an account with half a million followers noticing us! They said they loved what we do, wanted to genuinely support us, and hoped we could help introduce the ORIGINAL TEDDY SOFA to our customers, too. So here we are! Thank you so much for your kindness and support! We are grateful. The right people will find you. The right sofa will find you. Lots of love to Copenhagen! #maisonnayavienna #omhucph #thaispecialtycoffee #livingroom #vienna

candidateAudit.text: The Unsafe+Sounds festival, held annually in Vienna, returns in September with a kaleidoscopic program, offering a multifaceted glimpse into the contemporary music scene and AIL is delighted to once again host one event in the program. unsafeandsounds AIL, Otto Wagner-Postsparkasse / Georg-Coch-Platz 2, 1010 Vienna (Free entry) Overview: 18:30 Panel Discussion, unsafe+sounds in cooperation with the Weibel Institute for Digital Cultures (University of Applied Arts Vienna) weibel.institute Affective Histories Timotheus Vermeulen and Christian Höller in conversation with Sophie Publig History is never simply given. It is made through the scales and materials by which the past becomes legible: from sweeping narratives and historical events to gestures, sounds, images, technical infrastructures, and seemingly minor traces SOPHIE PUBLIG is a Senior Scientist researching digital ecosystems. Based at the Weibel Institute for Digital Cultures at the University of Applied Arts Vienna, she navigates the intricate networks of online territories. TIMOTHEUS VERMEULEN is Professor of Media, Culture and Society at the University of Oslo and joint director of the Media Aesthetics Research Group. He was a visiting scholar in Art History at Harvard in 2023–24 and will serve as joint Principal Investigator on a project on the politics of tone at the Centre for Advanced Study in Oslo in 2027–28. CHRISTIAN HÖLLER is editor and co-publisher of springerin – Hefte für Gegenwartskunst. Since 2024 he is head of the department Cross Disciplinary Strategies at the University of Applied Arts Vienna. cro

candidateAudit.text: OUR PRE-GRAND OPENING ART EXHIBITION STARTS WITH OUR NEIGHBOUR! CONSTANTIN SIMON is a Vienna-based artist creating paintings and sculptures around the topic of what art is in the 21st century involving fundamental science and what our function as humans is (becoming). His former series "Astronimals" and the "Freud's Dreams" art installation at Burning Man 2022 explored the transcendence of technology, spirit and nature. His new series"From Singularity to Complexity" focuses not only on where we are going, but especially on where we are coming from and what unites us. Principles of this exhibition are universal, and singularity can be found in every complexity: Thailand-rooted Maison Naya and Viennese Constantin Simon, unconnected at first glance, are direct neighbours. (see the last slide where Constantin put post-it on our window in February 2026-we didn't know each other back then. Now we finally found him) At their intersection, a shared wall (literally), lies this exhibition space. Even the visitors bring their complexity to this single focal point in time before spreading out in all directions again. "From Singularity to Complexity" by Constantin Simon: -Monday-Saturday -09:00-18:00 - 4th September - 2nd October 2026 - S I R I | SPACE at MAISON NAYA - Free entry See you soon! #maisonnayavienna #art #artexhibition #vienna

candidateAudit.text: Throughout August and September, the artist duo MUELLER-DIVJAK is residing at AIL for Summer Studio – using the space for artistic research, experimentation, and learning, developing the project's multisensory scenography – the so-called SΫS SPACE. Aim of the Summer Studio is to prepare the prototype of the scenography, which will be established at the AIL in June 2027 as the centerpiece of the final exhibition of the PEEK project ’SENSING LIVING SYSTEMS — Exploring the Potentials of Multisensory Scenography for Systems Awareness.’ The SΫS SPACE facilitates a physical experience of one's own embededdness within living systems, within complex interrelationships – within a greater whole. It paves the way for relational sensing and thinking – an embodied systems awareness, that can help in coping with complexity, challenges, and uncertainties, and in making good decisions towards sustainable futures. It deliberately reduces the dominance of the sense of sight, placing the emphasis instead on smell, touch, and hearing. Numerous scientists, as well as invited artists, politicians, journalists, children, senior citizens, curators, cultural workers, educators, and teenagers are individually guided through the immersive environment by Jeanette Müller and Paul Divjak and share their responses in photo-based reflections and semi-structured interviews. Their feedback directly informs the prototype. Save the date! 14 and 15 Sep 2026 The SΫS SPACE will open to the public in individual time slots for an exclusive multisensory experience. candidateAudit.text: DARIA Today 15.8.2026 is a big day for our little café. It is Daria's last shift. Daria started working with us from the beginning, pre-opening time in winter. We've been working together happily for 7 months. Daria is our Ukrainian darling girl who is smart, confident, honest, hard-working and, the most important quality when we chose our team member, kind. She has a passion in specialty coffee. She is a very fast learner about everything in coffee with our best in-house coffee trainer. Daria has a dream to become a psychologist and help people. During working with us she is preparing herself for a university. It is not easy. She has been trying since the first day we met her. Until last month. She got accepted into a very good university in the UK. We are very happy for her but we are sad too. We will miss making coffee with her, opening the shifts, closing the shifts and mopping the floor together (the last task we guess she will not miss it) To Daria, it's been a pleasure to work with you. We are very proud of you. We are confident that you will have a wonderful future and become a very good psychologist that can help many people. Come back to visit us sometimes. Now go catch your dream! We don't say goodbye. We say see you again. Auf Wiedersehen. ❤️ Love Naya, Pahparn & MAISON NAYA team 15.8.2026 Wien #maisonnayavienna #teamwork #farewell

candidateAudit.title: The exhibition [REVERBERATED]. Following the Movement of Memory is still running till this Friday, July 10! Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 Last guided tour: Thur, July 9, 17:00 Memory is not
candidateAudit.text: The exhibition [REVERBERATED]. Following the Movement of Memory is still running till this Friday, July 10! Mon–Fri: 11:00–18:00 Last guided tour: Thur, July 9, 17:00 Memory is not a stable record of the past. Rather than functioning as a static archive, it unfolds as a dynamic process in which traces are continuously reshaped by perception, narration, and material conditions. Across these artistic approaches, [REVERBERATED] invites visitors to consider memory not as something simply preserved, but as something continuously produced through interactions between bodies, technologies, and environments. The exhibition thus explores how the past continues to reverberate within the systems of the present. With contributions by: Agustina Belén Agüero, Lobna Awidat, Phin Anibal, Rimon Alyagon Darr, Ronnie Danaher, Tatiana Del Valle, Hasti Ghasedi, Leah Barbara Mukui Giertz, Hanna Hofmann, Tal Horesh, Mauritius Itzinger, Laura Isselhorst, Dina Karaman, Moritz Klarer, Anna Buchner, Leonard Otterbein, David Ristić, Rajarshi Sarkar, Agnes Schyberg, Aryan Shahabian, Majedeh Shahvelayati, Mehrta Shirzadian, Pauline Simon, Laura Chalabi, People of Soil Photos: Lea Dörl

candidateAudit.title: A new series of postcards is now installed at Café Exchange cafe_exchange The series was extracted from the course ‘Drawing: Here & Now’ by Simon Goritschnig zeichnungunddruckgrafi
candidateAudit.text: A new series of postcards is now installed at Café Exchange cafe_exchange The series was extracted from the course ‘Drawing: Here & Now’ by Simon Goritschnig zeichnungunddruckgrafik In collaborative drawing, two people share a single pen – the line becomes a space of negotiation. A play between control and letting go. Who leads – and when? Impulse meets resistance, conviction meets empathy. Not always a conversation, but always an understanding – a dance on paper. These and other experiments are part of the course “Drawing: Here & Now” by Simon Goritschnig, in which students of the department Drawing and Printmaking explore various qualities of drawing beyond observational study. In the project “Reflex,” these experimental setups are set against observational drawing. Students draw in the cashier hall of the former Postsparkasse, intuitively picking up details from architecture and space, as well as situations of coming together: conversations, movements, gazes. In this process, it becomes visible how public and social space is visually probed and explored. The focus lies on reflection — with, through, and within drawing. With contributions by: Andrea Vairelles, Anna Marino, Beth Sorby, Emilia Schönwiese, Flora Schmid, Hannah Horn, Henriette Sonntag, Leo Hasslinger, Maria Lutkova, Max Offergeld, Nikolaus Kohout, Sophie Schweizer, Anija S Dartizio, Timo Pfeifer, Vera Kügel AIL in cooperation with the department Drawing and Printmaking and Simon Goritschnig Image: Henriette Sonntag Design: Atelier Dreibholz Concept Postcard Editions and Production: Eva Weber
